full_instruction: Write a fantasy story about a necromancer who takes on a young apprentice against her better judgment. The necromancer's tower is built from the bones of every creature she has ever raised and released. Write the story in past tense. Use a formal, archaic narrative voice. The story must be exactly six sentences long. During the story, reveal that the apprentice sought her out specifically to learn how to bring back a sibling who died years ago. Include the exact sentence "The dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking." End with the necromancer refusing to teach the final spell, choosing instead to adopt the apprentice as her own.

In the shadowy corners of Eldoria, where death whispered in every corner and darkness thrived, lived Morwen—a notorious necromancer feared by all yet respected by none. Her reputation for ruthlessness was as terrifying as her magic; it echoed through the land like thunder after a storm. One day, while traversing Shadowmere forest alone, she stumbled upon young Alric whose wide eyes betrayed his fear amidst looming shadows reaching out menacingly towards him.

Morwen sensed an unusual surge of energy emanating from this lad; it was potent and raw, unlike anything she'd encountered before. Against her better judgment—an instinct honed over years steeped in dark arts—she resolved to take him under her wing hoping that this newfound apprentice might satiate the insatiable thirst for power that had consumed her life.

As weeks turned into months, their bond grew stronger; they spent countless hours studying ancient texts on arcane arts and experimenting with various spells despite herself growing fond of this impetuous apprentice who reminded her so much of herself when first starting out—impulsive fearless hungry for knowledge. However amidst their studies lay a secret unspoken between them: Alric sought her out specifically to learn how bring back his sibling who died years ago—a desperate plea borne from grief-stricken heartstrings yearning desperately for reunion lost too soon.
